Settings.heading: Settings
Settings.subtitle: Every number here drives the store and management screens — change it here instead of in code.
Settings.warningsSubtitle: Days without a sale before a product is flagged. Already live on both the store and management screens. One shared ladder for now — per-subcategory tuning comes once products carry a subcategory tag.
Settings.slowMovingDaysHint: Stored for Ranch/backend to use when classifying a product Slow vs. Dead — this app doesn't compute that classification itself, it just displays whatever status the task data carries.
Settings.shelfLifeSubtitle: Default shelf life per fresh subcategory, in days.
Settings.shelfLifeNotConnected: Not wired up yet: products don't carry a subcategory tag yet, so these numbers aren't used anywhere in the app. They'll take effect once the management screen rework (Step 8) tags each product.
Settings.bestTodaySubtitle: Discount tiers and their price codes. Live on the store screen's price-to-sell buttons and confirm dialog — editing a tier here updates them immediately.
Settings.tasksSubtitle: Daily task list limits on the store screen.
Settings.maxPerDayHint: Live: caps today's task list on the store screen (sorted by Rupiah value, highest first), rest shows up tomorrow.
Settings.checklistItemCountHint: How many items show when staff tap "Start check" (Step 4) — not applied yet, the Check list flow doesn't exist yet.
Settings.transferSubtitle: Distance limits and minimum value for moving stock between stores.
Settings.quickHopKmHint: Live: distance up to this counts as "quick hop" in the store screen's move-to-store confirm dialog (Step 6).
Settings.vanRunKmHint: Live: distance beyond quick hop and up to this counts as "van run"; further than this shows as "too far" (Step 6).
Settings.minValueMultiplierHint: Not active yet — comes with the full "Stock in the right store" tab (Step 5).
Settings.maintainMinDisplayLabel: Keep minimum display stock at the sending store
Settings.featureFlagsSubtitle: Turning features on per store, by date, is handled in a follow-up task.
